article.title: 阅读三 · 梦境与情绪调节
article.background: 心理与神经科学解释。把梦从“不可控噪音”推进为可能参与情绪调节、甚至可被训练控制的心理过程。

sentences.en: Of all the components of a good night’s sleep, dreams seem to be least within our control.
sentences.zh: 在一夜好眠的诸多组成部分中，梦似乎最不受我们控制。

sentences.en: In dreams, a window opens into a world where logic is suspended and dead people speak.
sentences.zh: 梦中仿佛有一扇窗打开，通向一个逻辑失效、逝者开口说话的世界。

sentences.en: A century ago, Freud formulated his revolutionary theory that dreams were the disguised shadows of our unconscious desires and fears; by the late 1970s, neurologists had switched to thinking of them as just “mental noise” — the random byproducts of the neural-repair work that goes on during sleep.
sentences.zh: 一个世纪前，弗洛伊德提出革命性理论，认为梦是无意识欲望与恐惧乔装后的影子；到了20世纪70年代末，神经学家却转而把梦视为“精神噪音”，即睡眠中神经修复工作的随机副产品。

sentences.en: Now researchers suspect that dreams are part of the mind’s emotional thermostat, regulating moods while the brain is “offline.”
sentences.zh: 如今，研究人员怀疑梦是心灵“情绪恒温器”的一部分，在大脑“离线”时调节情绪。

segments.text: Now researchers suspect that dreams are part of the mind’s emotional thermostat, regulating moods while the brain is “offline.”

sentences.en: And one leading authority says that these intensely powerful mental events can be not only harnessed but actually brought under conscious control, to help us sleep and feel better.
sentences.zh: 一位权威专家甚至认为，这些力量强大的心理事件不仅可以加以利用，还能被有意识地控制，从而帮助我们睡得更好、感觉更好。

segments.text: And one leading authority says that these intensely powerful mental events can be not only harnessed but actually brought under conscious control, to help us sleep and feel better.

sentences.en: “It’s your dream,” says Rosalind Cartwright, chair of psychology at Chicago’s Medical Center. “If you don’t like it, change it.”
sentences.zh: 芝加哥医学中心心理学系主任罗莎琳德·卡特赖特说：“这是你的梦。你不喜欢，就改变它。”

sentences.en: Evidence from brain imaging supports this view.
sentences.zh: 脑成像证据支持这一观点。

segments.text: Evidence from brain imaging supports this view.

sentences.en: The brain is as active during REM sleep — when most vivid dreams occur — as it is when fully awake, says Dr. Eric Nofzinger at the University of Pittsburgh.
sentences.zh: 匹兹堡大学的埃里克·诺夫辛格博士指出，在快速眼动睡眠期——大多数鲜明梦境发生于此——大脑的活跃程度与完全清醒时相当。

segments.text: The brain is as active during REM sleep — when most vivid dreams occur — as it is when fully awake, says Dr. Eric Nofzinger at the University of Pittsburgh.

sentences.en: But not all parts of the brain are equally involved; the limbic system, the “emotional brain,” is especially active, while the prefrontal cortex, the center of intellect and reasoning, is relatively quiet.
sentences.zh: 但大脑各部分参与程度并不相同：被称为“情绪脑”的边缘系统尤其活跃，而负责智力与推理的前额叶皮层则相对安静。

sentences.en: “We wake up from dreams happy or depressed, and those feelings can stay with us all day,” says Stanford sleep researcher Dr. William Dement.
sentences.zh: 斯坦福睡眠研究者威廉·德门特博士说：“我们从梦中醒来时可能快乐，也可能沮丧，而这些感受会伴随我们一整天。”

sentences.en: The link between dreams and emotions shows up among the patients in Cartwright’s clinic.
sentences.zh: 梦与情绪之间的联系，在卡特赖特诊所的患者身上体现得很明显。

sentences.en: Most people seem to have more bad dreams early in the night, progressing toward happier ones before awakening, suggesting that they are working through negative feelings generated during the day.
sentences.zh: 大多数人在前半夜似乎恶梦更多，临近醒来时梦境逐渐愉快，这表明人们可能正在梦中消化白天产生的负面情绪。

segments.text: Most people seem to have more bad dreams early in the night, progressing toward happier ones before awakening, suggesting that they are working through negative feelings generated during the day.

sentences.en: Because our conscious mind is occupied with daily life, we don’t always think about the emotional significance of the day’s events — until, it appears, we begin to dream.
sentences.zh: 由于清醒时的意识忙于日常生活，我们未必会思考当天事件的情绪意义——直到开始做梦，这种处理似乎才真正发生。

segments.text: Because our conscious mind is occupied with daily life, we don’t always think about the emotional significance of the day’s events — until, it appears, we begin to dream.

sentences.en: And this process need not be left to the unconscious.
sentences.zh: 而这一过程并非只能交给无意识。

sentences.en: Cartwright believes one can exercise conscious control over recurring bad dreams.
sentences.zh: 卡特赖特认为，人能够有意识地控制反复出现的恶梦。

sentences.en: As soon as you awaken, identify what is upsetting about the dream.
sentences.zh: 一醒来，就找出梦中究竟什么让你不安。
prosody_focus: As soon as you awaken, identify what is upsetting about the dream.

segments.text: As soon as you awaken, identify what is upsetting about the dream.

sentences.en: Visualize how you would like it to end instead; the next time it occurs, try to wake up just enough to control its course.
sentences.zh: 设想一个你希望它拥有的结局；下次梦境重现时，试着让自己清醒到足以控制它的发展。

sentences.en: With much practice people can learn to, literally, do it in their sleep.
sentences.zh: 经过大量练习，人们真的可以学会“在睡梦中”做到这一点。

sentences.en: At the end of the day, there’s probably little reason to pay attention to our dreams at all unless they keep us from sleeping or “we wake up in a panic,” Cartwright says.
